questions.question: [Medical Coding (Pharma) • Test 1 • Q1] When mapping a clinical trial adverse event description to MedDRA, which structural hierarchy level represents the most specific and lowest level term used for coding single verbatim reports?
options: Preferred Term (PT)
Lowest Level Term (LLT)
High Level Term (HLT)
System Organ Class (SOC)
questions.correctAnswer: Lowest Level Term (LLT)
questions.explanation: The Lowest Level Term (LLT) in MedDRA provides the maximum level of detail and is the level closest to the verbatim reporter's actual terminology, mapping directly to a single Preferred Term (PT).
questions.hint: Think about the bottom-most granularity of the MedDRA dictionary hierarchy.
questions.relatedConcept: MedDRA Terminology Hierarchy
questions.interviewTip: Interviviewers look for precise understanding of dictionary levels when handling raw clinical data verbatim entries.

questions.question: [Medical Coding (Pharma) • Test 1 • Q2] In pharmaceutical coding workflows compliant with ICH guidelines, what is the primary regulatory purpose of utilizing WHO Drug Global dictionary conventions for concomitant medications?
options: To calculate direct pharmaceutical manufacturing costs per clinical trial site
To determine the precise pharmacokinetic half-life of investigational medicinal products
To standardize active ingredient and trade name nomenclature for consistent safety signal detection
To automatically generate electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) database table schemas
questions.correctAnswer: To standardize active ingredient and trade name nomenclature for consistent safety signal detection
questions.explanation: WHO Drug Global is standardly used to code concomitant medications and investigational products into unified active ingredients and standardized drug codes to facilitate robust pharmacovigilance and signal detection across clinical studies.
questions.hint: Consider why regulatory agencies require standardized drug dictionaries rather than raw text.
questions.relatedConcept: WHO Drug Global Coding Standards
questions.interviewTip: Expect questions on how coding dictionaries support downstream safety and statistical reporting.

questions.question: [Medical Coding (Pharma) • Test 1 • Q3] In the context of the ICH E2B(R3) standard for Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs), how are null or unknown date values handled when only the year and month are known?
options: The missing day is automatically imputed as '01' with a separate flag indicating partial date entry.
The entire date field is left blank, and the information must be captured solely within the narrative field.
The missing components are filled with '99' to signify an unknown value following legacy FDA guidelines.
The day component is omitted, and the format is truncated to YYYY-MM according to the ISO 8601 subset specified by HL7/ICH.
questions.correctAnswer: The day component is omitted, and the format is truncated to YYYY-MM according to the ISO 8601 subset specified by HL7/ICH.
questions.explanation: ICH E2B(R3) adopts the HL7 Datum/Time data type where partial dates are represented by omitting the unknown lower granularity components (e.g., YYYY-MM for an unknown day), rather than using numeric fillers like '99'.
questions.hint: Think about how modern HL7-based XML standards handle granularity in partial timestamps.
questions.relatedConcept: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR data standards and partial date formatting
questions.interviewTip: Be prepared to discuss differences between legacy E2B(R2) representations (which sometimes used specific null flavors or placeholder characters) and the strict ISO 8601 subset enforced by E2B(R3).

questions.question: [Medical Coding (Pharma) • Test 1 • Q4] When mapping adverse event verbatim terms to the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA), what is the hierarchical level immediately above the Preferred Term (PT)?
options: High Level Term (HLT)
System Organ Class (SOC)
Lowest Level Term (LLT)
High Level Group Term (HLGT)
questions.correctAnswer: High Level Term (HLT)
questions.explanation: MedDRA's hierarchy from bottom to top is: LLT -> PT -> HLT -> HLGT -> SOC. Therefore, the level immediately above Preferred Term (PT) is High Level Term (HLT).
questions.hint: Recall the five levels of the MedDRA hierarchy and their bottom-up ordering.
questions.relatedConcept: MedDRA Terminology Hierarchy and Coding Rules
questions.interviewTip: Intermediary levels like HLT and HLGT are frequently tested to ensure the candidate understands multi-axial classification and grouping structures within pharmacovigilance databases.

questions.question: [UI/UX (Design) • Test 1 • Q1] In digital product design, what is the primary benefit of established typographic scales (Type Scale)?
options: Minimizes the download size of TTF font files.
Prevents CSS layout reflows on mobile devices.
Creates distinct visual hierarchy that guides scanning eyes from primary titles to metadata efficiently.
Enforces monochromatic color palettes across all screens.
questions.correctAnswer: Creates distinct visual hierarchy that guides scanning eyes from primary titles to metadata efficiently.
questions.explanation: A harmonic type scale (e.g., Major Third 1.25 or Golden Ratio 1.618) establishes intuitive relationships between headers, subheads, and body copy.
questions.hint: Harmonic font scale guides scannability and visual flow.
questions.relatedConcept: UI/UX (Design) - Typographic Hierarchy & Visual Scanning
questions.interviewTip: Maintain high line-height (1.5 - 1.6) on body text to maximize reading comfort.

questions.question: [UI/UX (Design) • Test 1 • Q2] What does Fitts's Law predict about user interaction with on-screen target elements?
options: The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
Users can hold at most 7 items in short-term memory (Miller's Law).
Decision time increases logarithmically with number of choices (Hick's Law).
Users perceive objects close together as belonging to the same group.
questions.correctAnswer: The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
questions.explanation: Fitts's law dictates that primary call-to-action buttons should be larger and closer to the user's cursor/thumb reach zone.
questions.hint: Target size and distance dictate acquisition time.
questions.relatedConcept: UI/UX (Design) - Fitts's Law in Interface Usability
questions.interviewTip: Screen corners and edges have infinite theoretical width because cursor cannot overshoot them.

questions.question: [UI/UX (Design) • Test 1 • Q3] According to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA), what is the minimum contrast ratio required for standard body text?

4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
10:1 strictly across dark mode interfaces.
questions.correctAnswer: 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
questions.explanation: WCAG AA compliance mandates at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text to ensure readability for users with moderate visual impairments.
questions.hint: 4.5:1 for standard text; 3:1 for large text.

questions.interviewTip: Never rely on color alone to convey error states or interactive affordances.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q1] When exporting a vector illustration from Adobe Illustrator to a raster format for web display, a graphic designer notices that all diagonal lines and text edges appear heavily pixelated and jagged. What is the primary cause of this visual defect?
options: The color mode was inadvertently set to CMYK instead of RGB.
The export settings lacked anti-aliasing, failing to blend edge pixels with the background.
The document resolution was locked at 300 PPI instead of 72 PPI.
The vector paths were inadvertently converted to compound shapes.
questions.correctAnswer: The export settings lacked anti-aliasing, failing to blend edge pixels with the background.
questions.explanation: Anti-aliasing smooths out the jagged appearance of diagonal and curved lines in raster images by creating a transition of intermediate color pixels along the edges. Without it, hard pixel stair-stepping occurs.
questions.hint: Think about how software smooths pixel boundaries when converting vector curves to a grid.
questions.relatedConcept: Rasterization and Anti-aliasing
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to check if candidates understand the fundamental difference between vector and raster rendering limitations on screen.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q2] A designer working in layout software applies a drop shadow to an object, but a harsh, solid block of grey appears behind the object instead of a soft, gradient-faded shadow. What does this specific symptom indicate about the effect settings?
options: The opacity of the drop shadow is set to 100%.
The blend mode of the shadow is set to Normal instead of Multiply.
The blur radius (or feathering) is set to zero or too low of a value.
The offset distance is too large relative to the canvas size.
questions.correctAnswer: The blur radius (or feathering) is set to zero or too low of a value.
questions.explanation: The softness or blur of a drop shadow is directly controlled by the blur or feather parameter. A setting of zero produces a sharp, unblurred silhouette of the object.
questions.hint: Consider which parameter controls the spread or softness of a shadow's edges.
questions.relatedConcept: Digital Effects and Blur Parameters
questions.interviewTip: Tests practical troubleshooting skills regarding basic graphic design software effects and parameter configuration.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q3] In typography, what does the term 'kerning' specifically refer to?
options: The uniform spacing applied across an entire block of text or word
The vertical distance measured between two consecutive baselines of type
The overall height of capital letters relative to the baseline
The adjustment of spacing between a specific pair of individual characters
questions.correctAnswer: The adjustment of spacing between a specific pair of individual characters
questions.explanation: Kerning is the selective adjustment of space between specific pairs of characters (such as 'AV' or 'To') to achieve a visually harmonious balance. Adjusting space across an entire block is tracking or letter-spacing, vertical distance is leading, and capital letter height is cap height.
questions.hint: Think about pairs of letters that look too far apart or too close together because of their geometric shapes.
questions.relatedConcept: Typography kerning vs tracking
questions.interviewTip: Designers frequently conflate kerning and tracking; testing this distinguishes fundamental vocabulary knowledge from guesswork.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q4] Which file format is specifically designed as a lossless vector graphic format standard for web publishing?
options: SVG
JPEG
PNG
GIF
questions.correctAnswer: SVG
questions.explanation: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is an XML-based vector image format for two-dimensional graphics that supports interactivity and animation, making it ideal for the web. JPEG and PNG are raster formats, and GIF is a bitmap format limited to 256 colors.
questions.hint: Look for the format that uses mathematical formulas (paths, curves) rather than pixels.
questions.relatedConcept: Vector vs raster file formats in web design
questions.interviewTip: Candidates must know when to deploy vector assets versus raster assets for responsive web design.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q5] A UI button’s text color is #FFFFFF on a background of #007BFF. The calculated contrast ratio is 4.6:1. According to WCAG AA guidelines, is this button’s text color acceptable for normal text?
options: No, because WCAG AA requires a contrast ratio of 7:1 for normal text.
Yes, because it meets the WCAG AA minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text.
Yes, because it meets the WCAG AA requirement for large text.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q6] What does DPI stand for and what does it primarily affect in printed media?
options: Dots per pixel – it controls screen brightness levels
Density per inch – it defines the file size of a document
Dots per inch – it determines the print resolution and sharpness of the output
Data per input – it influences network transfer speed
questions.correctAnswer: Dots per inch – it determines the print resolution and sharpness of the output
questions.explanation: DPI means Dots per Inch and refers to the number of ink dots a printer can place within one inch, directly affecting the sharpness and detail of printed material. The other options describe unrelated concepts.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q7] In print design, why is a bleed area added around a document before it is sent to a printer?
options: To provide extra space for binding the pages together
To increase the file size for higher‑resolution output
To embed the required fonts directly into the PDF
To ensure that background colors or images extend fully to the edge of the page after trimming
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure that background colors or images extend fully to the edge of the page after trimming
questions.explanation: A bleed adds extra margin (usually 1/8" to 1/4") beyond the final trim size so that any background or edge‑to‑edge elements continue past the cut line, preventing white borders. The other choices describe different concepts unrelated to bleed.
questions.hint: Consider what happens if the cut is slightly off‑center.
